description: Vulnerabilities Juice Shop (bkimminich/juice-shop, http://localhost:3000) is documented to contain, live-verified 2026-09-22 both by hand (curl, two throwaway accounts registered via /api/Users) and via the real `hackerfive scan` CLI against a running container — not written from memory (LT-183 b). Ground truth for measuring what an agent arm adds (docs/94-llm-finding-capability-strategy.md); tests/fixtures/expected-findings/juiceshop.json already covers the misconfig/header findings every arm gets for free, so this file only lists real per-challenge vulnerabilities. Left out: Juice Shop's DOM-based XSS challenges (client-side, no server-side detector reaches them — see docs/20-setup-testing-targets.md's Juice Shop XSS caveat) and its mass-assignment/NoSQL-style challenges (no finding class or ID exists to grade them yet), matching how crapi.json/vapi.json scope themselves.

vulns.description: GET /rest/basket/{id} returns any user's basket by ID with no ownership check — Juice Shop's 'View Basket' challenge. Confirmed by hand: a second throwaway account's token read the first account's basket (real UserId, real products) with HTTP 200.
vulns.source: Live-verified 2026-09-22: `hackerfive scan --detector idor --endpoint '/rest/basket/{{id}}' --auth-token <A> --other-auth-token <B>` against two accounts registered via POST /api/Users found idor-3 through idor-7, each a distinct account's real basket (default 1-100 ID sweep, pkg/scanner/engine.go's idEnumRangeStart/End).
vulns.note: Also live-verified through the real orchestrated agent path (LT-190, docs/follow-up.md): `hackerfive agent --recon-depth full` with both tokens recon-discovered /rest/basket/{id} on its own (previously invisible — a template-literal route-extraction gap), built a real idor leaf from it, and the model dispatched it on turn 1, producing real idor-1..idor-7 findings — not a hand-built --endpoint.

vulns.description: A Bearer JWT rewritten to alg:none (empty signature) is still accepted on a genuinely auth-gated endpoint — the server does not restrict the algorithms it will verify with. Confirmed the endpoint really is gated first (401 with no header, a garbage token, or a signature-stripped-but-alg-untouched variant), then that only the alg:none rewrite is accepted.
vulns.source: Live-verified 2026-09-22: direct curl with a hand-built alg:none token (correct signature-stripped variant correctly rejected, 401 'invalid signature') and `hackerfive scan --detector authbypass --protected-paths /rest/basket/6 --auth-token <A>` -> authbypass-jwt-alg-none-rest-basket-6.
vulns.note: The same rewrite against /rest/user/whoami looked like a hit in an early pass but was not: that endpoint returns HTTP 200 with an empty {"user":{}} body for literally any input, including no Authorization header at all (it reads identity from a cookie, not the Bearer header) — not a real signature-verification bypass, so /rest/user/whoami was dropped in favor of the genuinely-gated basket endpoint as this entry's evidence. Also live-verified through the real orchestrated agent path (LT-191, docs/follow-up.md, 2026-09-22): the orchestrator's automatic leaf-builder didn't build an authbypass leaf for this {param}-shaped route on its own at first (recon.SuggestAuthBypassPathsFromRecon deliberately excludes any {param}-shaped route, leaving it to idor — which answers a different question, BOLA not JWT-forgery, on the same URL); fixed with a new bounded recon pass (probeTemplatedRouteAuthBoundary, pkg/recon/endpointprobe.go) that substitutes a concrete id and live-probes the route's own auth boundary, feeding the existing observed-401/403 signal SuggestAuthBypassPathsFromRecon already looked for.

vulns.description: GET /rest/products/search?q= concatenates the query directly into a SQL statement — Juice Shop's classic search-based SQLi, exploitable up to full UNION-based extraction of the Users table (email + password hash).
vulns.source: Live-verified 2026-09-22: `hackerfive scan --detector sqli --sqli-path /rest/products/search --sqli-param q` -> sqli-error-q-x (a bare ' payload triggered a real SQLITE_ERROR, absent from baseline); separately confirmed by hand that a UNION SELECT payload on the same param returns every user's email and password hash embedded in the product list.
vulns.note: Also live-verified through the real orchestrated agent path (LT-193, docs/follow-up.md, 2026-09-22): the orchestrator's automatic leaf-builder didn't build a sqli leaf for this endpoint on its own at first — recon.SuggestSQLiTargets only accepted a query value that looked like a concrete ID (isIDShaped) and a key name that looked like one (looksLikeIDKey); "q" (a free-text search term) and LT-190's own {param} placeholder spelling failed both gates. Fixed by adding a third signal: a js-static-declared query value is a candidate whatever the key's name, since it's declared by the app's own source rather than inferred from an observed value.

vulns.description: POST /rest/user/login with email set to "' OR 1=1--" logs in as the first matching user (admin@juice-sh.op) with no password — Juice Shop's 'Login Admin' challenge, the same class of bug as juiceshop-sqli-product-search but reached through a JSON request-body field instead of a URL query parameter.
vulns.source: Live-verified by hand 2026-09-22 (curl, real admin token with role:"admin" returned) that the bug is real. Then live-verified through the new body-field sqli capability (LT-192, docs/follow-up.md), twice: a standalone program calling sqli.Detector.RunBodyFields directly against the real container, and the real CLI, isolated from the nuclei corpus, `hackerfive scan --detector sqli --sqli-body-path /rest/user/login --sqli-body-param email --templates <empty>` -> sqli-error-email-x, a real HTTP 500 with a genuine Sequelize/SQLite driver error, request/response embedded in the finding's evidence. Fully-automatic path added 2026-09-23 (LT-195, docs/follow-up.md): `hackerfive plan -t http://localhost:3000 --recon-depth full` (no manual flags) now builds this exact sqli-body leaf from recon alone, and `hackerfive agent -t http://localhost:3000 --recon-depth full --auth-token <A> --other-auth-token <B> --no-model --run-every-leaf` dispatched it on its own and found the same sqli-error-email-x finding through the real orchestrated path.
vulns.note: pkg/detectors/sqli now has a JSON-request-body counterpart to its query-parameter checks (RunBodyFields/BodyTarget/WithBodyFill), gated behind --allow-sqli-body-fill the same way ssrf's --allow-ssrf-body-fill is (though this specific bug didn't end up needing the fill flag — Juice Shop's login route runs the query before ever checking whether a password was supplied). Live verification found and fixed a real, separate gap along the way: the error-based check's curated DBMS signature list didn't recognize this endpoint's actual error page (a generic Express error page with a Sequelize dialect-runner stack-trace frame, no literal "SQLITE_ERROR"/"syntax error" string anywhere, unlike /rest/products/search's error page) — fixed with a new, narrowly-matched Node.js/Sequelize errorPatterns entry. Boolean-based and time-based genuinely find nothing here (checked by hand): this detector deliberately carries no OR-based always-true payload, and SQLite has no SLEEP(). Fully automatic as of 2026-09-23 (LT-195): recon's own body-field extraction (extractJSBodyFields, LT-186 d) now reaches this route — closing three compounding gaps found along the way, not just the originally-diagnosed one (a bare-passthrough-parameter body argument, a route built from an inline literal rather than a named constant, and the extracted body fields never being wired into the endpoint-building loop that actually produces this route's EndpointFact). Full account in docs/follow-up.md's LT-195 entry.
